item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Mixed, leaning positive on social protection, food security, disaster resilience, and some education-related delivery. The evidence is weaker for health, water/sanitation, and housing access specifically, and the best counterevidence is that food affordability remained strained and one flagship rice intervention had limited pass-through.

**Claims**
- **PBBM issues EO No. 52, institutionalizing and expanding DSWD’s Pag-abot Program for street dwellers, other poor and vulnerable individuals** — Presidential Communications Office via PIA, Jan. 22, 2024: [link](https://mirror.pia.gov.ph/press-releases/2024/01/22/pbbm-issues-eo-no-52-institutionalizing-and-expanding-dswds-pag-abot-program-for-street-dwellers-other-poor-and-vulnerable-individuals)  
  Marcos institutionalized a cross-agency program for street dwellers and other poor/vulnerable people, including shelter, livelihood, employment, and social-safety-net support. This is direct evidence of expanded access to social protection and related services. `6B.2`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`.

- **DSWD expands social services under PBBM administration** — Presidential Communications Office, Jan. 12, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/dswd-expands-social-services-under-pbbm-administration/)  
  The administration said DSWD support was expanding because more people needed help, and Congress increased AKAP to aid low-wage workers coping with high prices. This supports a welfare/access finding, though it is official framing. `6B.2`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`.

- **PBBM calls for comprehensive national flood-control plan to protect communities, production areas** — Presidential Communications Office, Jul. 26, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-calls-for-comprehensive-national-flood-control-plan-to-protect-communities-production-areas/)  
  After Typhoon Carina and Habagat, Marcos ordered a national flood-control plan framed around protecting communities and production areas. This is strong evidence for resilience-oriented access to safe living conditions, which matters for water-related and sanitation-adjacent welfare. `6B.2`; also `5B.6`, `5B.9`.

- **4,700 flood control projects done under PBBM watch; over 4,000 under construction** — Presidential Communications Office, May 7, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/4700-flood-control-projects-done-under-pbbm-watch-over-4000-under-construction/)  
  The government emphasized large-scale flood mitigation as a public-works priority. This supports a limited infrastructure-access finding, though it is self-reported and does not prove equal distribution. `6B.2`; also `5B.6`, `5B.9`.

- **SWS survey: PBBM very good on helping disaster victims, improving children’s quality of education, helping the poor** — Presidential Communications Office, Sep. 14, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/sws-survey-pbbm-very-good-on-helping-disaster-victims-improving-childrens-quality-of-education-helping-the-poor/)  
  The administration highlighted survey evidence that Marcos scored strongly on disaster response, children’s education, and aid to the poor. This is one of the clearest broad signals of service-delivery improvement across vulnerable groups. `6B.2`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`.

- **Gov’t backs campaign to end violence against women** — Presidential Communications Office, Dec. 2, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-backs-campaign-to-end-violence-against-women/)  
  The administration backed a women’s-protection campaign framed around rights and safety across different backgrounds. This is relevant to access to social protection, especially for vulnerable women. `6B.2`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`.

- **DSWD touts gov’t efforts to end violence, abuse against women, children** — Presidential Communications Office, Dec. 11, 2024: [link](https://mirror.pco.gov.ph/news_releases/dswd-touts-govt-efforts-to-end-violence-abuse-against-women-children/)  
  DSWD described stronger referral, legal, medical, and shelter support for women and child survivors. This is concrete social-protection delivery, though it is narrower than a broad health/housing access reform. `6B.2`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`.

- **Marcos bans all POGOs after citing torture, kidnapping, trafficking, and murder** — GMA News Online, Jul. 22, 2024: [link](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/914272/marcos-announces-ban-on-all-pogo/story/)  
  The POGO ban targeted an abuse-linked sector that harmed workers, migrants, and other vulnerable people. That is an access/welfare-positive move because it reduced exposure to exploitation rather than protecting a politically connected industry. `6B.2`; also `6B.1`, `5B.5`, `5B.8`.

- **Philippines orders foreign workers in offshore gaming hubs to leave in 2 months** — Reuters via ThePrint, Jul. 24, 2024: [link](https://theprint.in/world/philippines-orders-foreign-workers-in-offshore-gaming-hubs-to-leave-in-2-months/2188594/)  
  Reuters described implementation of the shutdown after Marcos moved against operators tied to trafficking and scams. This reinforces the welfare-protection reading. `6B.2`; also `6B.1`, `5B.5`, `5B.8`.

- **PBBM inks law to further boost PH rice industry** — Presidential Communications Office, Dec. 9, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-inks-law-to-further-boost-ph-rice-industry/)  
  Extending and enlarging RCEF is a structural agriculture move aimed at productivity and farmer support. This is relevant to food security and rural livelihoods, not just short-term price optics. `6B.2`; also `5B.10`, `5B.8`.

- **President Marcos unveils DA’s Agri-Puhunan Program targeting 1.2 million hectares with low-cost credit and market support** — Department of Agriculture, Sep. 13, 2024: [link](https://www.da.gov.ph/president-marcos-unveils-das-agri-puhunan-program-targeting-1-2-million-hectares-with-low-cost-credit-and-market-support/)  
  The program provided low-cost credit, subsistence support, and market access for farmers. This is direct evidence of food-system and rural-access improvement. `6B.2`; also `5B.6`, `5B.8`.

- **2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Philippines** — U.S. Department of State via ecoi.net, 2024: [link](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html)  
  The report says the Marcos administration shifted the antidrug campaign toward treatment, due process, and rule-of-law investigations, and that killings declined versus prior years. This is relevant to welfare because it reduced some state-linked harm, though abuses continued. `6B.2`; also `6B.1`, `5B.9`, `6B.8`.

- **Philippine inflation quickens again in March as rice soars** — Reuters, Apr. 4, 2024: [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/philippine-inflation-quickens-again-in-march-as-rice-soars-3366872)  
  Rice inflation hit a 15-year high and the BSP stayed tight, showing that food access remained under severe pressure early in 2024. This is the clearest negative evidence against a clean “improved access” finding. `6B.2`; also `5B.9`, `5B.10`.

- **NEDA says reduced rice tariffs failed to lower prices** — GMA News Online, Dec. 10, 2024: [link](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/929579/neda-reduced-rice-tariffs-failed-to-lower-prices/story/)  
  NEDA said the tariff cut did not lower retail rice prices as anticipated. That undercuts the administration’s food-access claim, even if the DA argued the policy blunted an even worse spike. `6B.2`; also `5B.9`, `5B.10`.

- **Marcos opens 2024 SONA admitting rice prices are costly** — GMA News Online, Jul. 22, 2024: [link](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/914278/marcos-opens-2024-sona-admitting-rice-prices-are-costly/story/)  
  Marcos openly acknowledged that rice prices were painful for families. This is honest recognition of the access problem, but it also shows the problem remained unresolved. `6B.2`; also `5B.9`, `5B.10`.

- **Philippines: Dangerous “Red Tagging” of Labor Leaders** — Human Rights Watch, Sep. 25, 2024: [link](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders)  
  HRW says officials and security actors threatened union leaders and targeted women’s groups, Indigenous peoples, journalists, teachers, and judges. This does not directly measure service access, but it is strong negative evidence that vulnerable groups faced a coercive environment while trying to access rights and support. `6B.2`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`, `6B.8`.

- **Philippines: “I turned my fear into courage”** — Amnesty International, Oct. 14, 2024: [link](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8574/2024/en/)  
  Amnesty says Marcos-era actors weaponized digital tools, misinformation, and anti-terror framing to create fear for activists, journalists, teachers, and others. This is negative background evidence against broad, safe access to public welfare systems. `6B.2`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`, `6B.8`.

**Search Gap**
- I found solid evidence for food security, disaster resilience, and social protection.
- I found only indirect evidence for health access and almost no strong 2024 evidence on water, sanitation, or housing access specifically.
- So the best-supported conclusion is partial improvement in welfare access, not a comprehensive across-the-board gain.
